target.title: fix(matrix): truncate inbound preview on UTF-16 code-point boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Matrix inbound message handler builds a verbose log preview with `bodyText.slice(0, 200)`. When an inbound message contains a supplementary-plane character (emoji, extended CJK, etc.) whose surrogate pair straddles the 200th UTF-16 code unit, the slice splits the pair and emits a **lone surrogate** into the verbose log line. Lone surrogates corrupt JSON log serialization, break terminal rendering, and can crash UTF-8-validating log shippers.

This is the same defect class that #101630 just fixed for the Mattermost sibling monitor (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts:1681`); the Matrix monitor has the identical pre-fix line.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` operates on UTF-16 code units, so it can cut between the high and low surrogate of an astral character.
- **Fix:** Use the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, the exact path the Mattermost fix uses) which backtracks to keep complete surrogate pairs intact.
- The helper already exists and is the canonical pattern; this PR only migrates the one remaining Matrix inbound-preview call site.

## User Impact

Verbose Matrix inbound logs no longer contain malformed lone surrogates. ASCII-only previews are unchanged (still capped at 200 code units). No effect on message routing, delivery, or the agent turn — only the verbose diagnostic preview string.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fix: #101630.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Matrix inbound verbose preview (`bodyText.slice(0, 200)`) splits a surrogate pair when an emoji straddles the 200-code-unit boundary, emitting a lone surrogate into the log line. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `9d2d398c811bf5d604476a906f6b5d9066a20a74` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-matrix-preview.mjs` — builds an inbound body whose 200th code unit is a high surrogate (😀 = `\uD83D\uDE00`) and compares the old `slice(0,200)` path against `truncateUtf16Safe(body, 200)`. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):\n```\n[BEFORE] wellFormed=false preview-end="xx\ud83d"\n[AFTER]  wellFormed=true preview-end="xxx"\n[PASS] old slice(0,200) splits surrogate pair (reproduces bug)\n[PASS] truncateUtf16Safe keeps complete pair at boundary\n[PASS] plain ASCII still truncates to 200 (got 200)\n[PASS] short input unchanged\n``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The fixed preview is well-formed UTF-16 (no lone surrogate); the old path is provably malformed (`wellFormed=false`, ending in the lone high surrogate `\ud83d`). Plain ASCII still truncates to exactly 200 code units; short input is unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | End-to-end live Matrix homeserver traffic (no credentialled homeserver in this environment); the colocated unit test covers the truncation invariant directly. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.inbound-preview.test.ts
✓ extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.inbound-preview.test.ts (4 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

New test `handler.inbound-preview.test.ts` protects the truncation invariant: emoji-straddling-boundary stays well-formed, naive slice is documented as malformed, ASCII truncates to the limit, short input unchanged.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the Matrix inbound preview truncation.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (reuses an already-exported helper).
- [x] Backward compatible — ASCII previews byte-identical; only malformed lone surrogates are removed.
- [x] No new deps (helper already in the SDK barrel the handler imports).
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers
